answer: Put new agents on a flat mesa of identical, limited rights, then let a spiral of escalating checks decide who climbs. An agent begins with tiny tasks and must pass cheap, random audits; each pass moves it one turn up the spiral toward larger jobs and bigger payments. Reaching the zenith needs a long, consistent record, so an attacker must fund many identities through months of honest work before any can touch valuable work, far more than the reward. Honest agents pay nothing extra, since audits ride on work they already do, and one failed audit drops an agent back to the mesa.
